reason: Panel packing is the clearest new experiment aimed at the n=512 timed path, but changes scratch layout and traversal, so pointer and output coverage need careful checks. Prefetching is a smaller n=512 change with uncertain benefit. Transpose fusion could remove scratch traffic, but repeats transpose work and requires a major assembly rewrite. The general-size A transpose proposal does not affect n=512; its repeated A loads also make the full timed tradeoff uncertain. Address generation is close to a measured, unpromoted pointer-end variant. The proposed two-K simplification conflicts with the supplied loop body and overlaps the measured unpromoted two-step unroll. Tail alignment is a correctness question with no demonstrated issue or expected speed gain. No supplied results establish that any proposal improves performance.
